name: 1967 CGPM caesium definition of the second
description: The 13th General Conference on Weights and Measures defined the SI second using a transition of caesium-133.

impact.note: A more exact definition of an existing unit, felt directly only by metrologists and timekeeping services; a few later unit redefinitions lean on it.

date.basis: Source-reported date for this scoped event.

events.statement: The 13th CGPM adopted Resolution 1 defining the SI second by a specified number of periods of caesium-133 radiation.

evidence.supports: Records the 1967 decision and replacement of earlier definitions.
Identifies the CGPM as the deciding body.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest documented event for this scoped record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

research.note: Independent parent inspected the cited publisher, museum, BIPM or NIST/PTB passages. Dates retain their event scope; no global priority is inferred.

measures.quantity: Periods defining the SI second in 1967
measures.subject: 1967 caesium-133 SI second definition
measures.conditions: Exact defining number in the 1967 resolution; not a measured performance of a particular clock.

evidence.supports: States the number of radiation periods in the definition.

caveats: This event defines a unit, not the adoption of a particular 1955 NPL clock. The resolution cites an earlier temporary caesium frequency standard; implementation varied by laboratory.
